items.stem: Enzymes increase the rate of biochemical reactions primarily by:

options.text: Lowering the activation energy of the reaction
options.rationale: Correct: enzymes reduce the activation-energy barrier, speeding the reaction.

options.text: Increasing the activation energy of the reaction
options.rationale: Raising activation energy would slow, not speed, the reaction.

options.text: Changing the overall free-energy difference between reactants and products
options.rationale: Enzymes do not change the net energy of reactants and products.

options.text: Being consumed permanently in the reaction
options.rationale: Enzymes are catalysts and are not consumed by the reaction.

items.explanation: Correct: enzymes reduce the activation-energy barrier, speeding the reaction.
items.domain_ref: Chemistry of Life and Cell Structure

items.stem: In double-stranded DNA, adenine pairs with:

options.rationale: Correct: adenine pairs with thymine (A-T) in DNA.
Guanine pairs with cytosine, not adenine.
Cytosine pairs with guanine, not adenine.
Bases pair complementarily; adenine does not pair with adenine.

items.explanation: Correct: adenine pairs with thymine (A-T) in DNA.

items.stem: Which TWO conditions are required for natural selection to change a population over time?

options.rationale: Correct: traits must be heritable for selection to act across generations.

options.text: Differential reproductive success linked to that variation
options.rationale: Correct: some variants must leave more offspring than others.
No variation means natural selection has nothing to act on.

options.text: Acquired traits always being passed to offspring
options.rationale: Selection acts on heritable, not merely acquired, traits.
Selection does not require an unchanging infinite environment.

items.explanation: Correct keys: A, B. Correct: traits must be heritable for selection to act across generations. Correct: some variants must leave more offspring than others.
